How It Works

How Professional Maintenance Works

Our maintenance process follows a systematic, six-step protocol designed to maximize pathogen elimination and provide verifiable documentation of results. Every step is performed by trained, background-checked technicians.

1
Issue Identification

Maintenance needs are identified through scheduled inspections, cleaning crew observations (our janitorial teams flag issues during nightly cleaning), tenant work orders, or emergency calls. Every request is logged in our digital work order system.

2
Assessment and Prioritization

Each issue is assessed for urgency (emergency, urgent, routine, or scheduled), scope, and required skills. Emergency issues (active leaks, safety hazards, security concerns) receive same-day response. Routine items are scheduled within the next service visit.

3
Skilled Technician Dispatch

A trained maintenance technician with the appropriate skills and tools is dispatched to your facility. Our technicians carry standard parts, hardware, and supplies to resolve most common issues in a single visit without return trips.

4
Repair and Resolution

The technician completes the repair, replacement, or maintenance task according to manufacturer specifications and applicable building codes. Work that exceeds our scope (major electrical, structural, licensed plumbing) is identified and referred to appropriate licensed contractors.

5
Quality Check

Completed work is inspected to verify proper function, appearance, and safety. The technician tests repaired fixtures, verifies proper operation, and ensures the work area is clean and restored.

6
Documentation

Every maintenance event is documented in JaniTrack with before-and-after photos, work performed, parts used, and time spent. This documentation creates a maintenance history for each building system — valuable for budgeting, asset management, and warranty tracking.

FAQ

Maintenance FAQ — Spring Valley, NY

Common questions about maintenance services in Spring Valley.

What is commercial facility maintenance?+
Commercial facility maintenance is the professional upkeep, repair, and preservation of building systems, fixtures, and infrastructure in commercial environments. It covers light plumbing, electrical fixture maintenance, HVAC filter replacement, painting, door and hardware repair, furniture assembly, and general handyman services. Professional maintenance prevents small issues from becoming costly emergencies and preserves building value.
What types of repairs do you handle?+
We handle light plumbing (leaky faucets, running toilets, clogged drains), electrical (light fixture replacement, outlet and switch repairs, ballast replacement), HVAC (filter changes, thermostat issues, vent cleaning), carpentry (door adjustments, lock hardware, cabinet repairs), painting (touch-ups, accent walls, common area refreshes), and general handyman tasks (furniture assembly, picture hanging, caulking, weather stripping). Work requiring licensed contractors is identified and referred.
Do you offer 24/7 emergency maintenance?+
Yes. We provide 24/7 emergency response for urgent facility issues including active water leaks, electrical failures, broken windows or doors, HVAC failures in extreme weather, and security concerns. Emergency calls are answered live and a technician is dispatched based on the urgency level — typically within 2-4 hours for true emergencies.
Can I bundle maintenance with janitorial service?+
Yes, and most clients do. Bundling cleaning and maintenance under GreenPoint provides single-vendor simplicity, discounted pricing (typically 15-25% less than separate contractors), proactive issue identification from cleaning crews, and coordinated scheduling that reduces total disruption to your facility. Bundled clients also receive priority scheduling for maintenance requests.
How much does commercial facility maintenance cost?+
Maintenance is typically priced as a monthly retainer based on building size, age, and expected service volume, or on a per-call basis for facilities with intermittent needs. Monthly retainers for a typical 25,000-50,000 sq ft building range from $500-$2,000 depending on scope. Per-call pricing ranges from $75-$150 per visit plus materials. Bundling with janitorial service reduces both the maintenance cost and total facility management overhead.
What maintenance tasks are outside your scope?+
We refer to licensed specialists for major electrical work (panel upgrades, new circuits), major plumbing (main line repairs, water heater replacement), structural repairs, roofing, elevator maintenance, fire suppression systems, and any work requiring specific state licensure. We coordinate with these specialists on your behalf when needed, maintaining single-point-of-contact simplicity.
